A viable non-LLM core is emerging: render the page in a controlled browser context, extract a deterministic scene graph from the live DOM/computed styles, then create native Penpot boards, text, shapes, and images through the plugin API. The opt-in script choice makes isolation a first-class requirement. A nested sandbox can run the pasted document without giving it Penpot API access, but a purely browser-only build cannot reliably rasterize cross-origin fonts/images when an asset server lacks CORS. We therefore need to decide whether v1 stays fully local with graceful fallbacks, or introduces an asset/render service for higher fidelity.

There’s also a separate editability choice: preserving CSS flex/grid as Penpot layout is powerful, but exact browser coordinates are more faithful. The importer can combine them, but one needs to be the default.

content.text:
One technical caveat surfaced before I finalize: browser sandboxing isolates permissions and Penpot access, but it does not guarantee CPU isolation. An intentionally infinite loop in opted-in page JavaScript can still hang the plugin/tab before a timeout handler runs. With the browser-only architecture, script execution can be safe from Penpot data access, but only best-effort against resource exhaustion.

That combination is still workable if the UI labels script execution “trusted source only” and defaults it off; I just don’t want the plan to imply a hard timeout the browser cannot enforce.

<proposed_plan>
# Ultimate HTML-to-Penpot Extension

## Summary

Build a deterministic, browser-only Penpot plugin that converts one pasted HTML page into editable Penpot designs without an LLM or hosted rendering service.

- Render HTML/CSS in an isolated iframe and extract computed layout into a versioned scene graph.
- Create separate full-page boards for Desktop `1440×900`, Tablet `768×1024`, and Mobile `390×844`; allow custom viewport presets.
- Favor responsive editability: translate compatible flex/grid layouts into Penpot layouts, then use measured positioning where translation would be unsafe.
- Use native text, boards, shapes, SVG, and images whenever possible; use localized raster fallbacks when browser access permits, otherwise create labeled placeholders with diagnostics.
- Require only Penpot’s `content:write` permission. The supported API provides the required shape factories, media upload, layout, plugin-data, and UI messaging capabilities. ([Penpot API](https://doc.plugins.penpot.app/interfaces/Penpot), [plugin architecture](https://help.penpot.app/plugins/getting-started/))

## Implementation

### Plugin foundation and UI

- Scaffold React, TypeScript, Vite, Penpot plugin styles/types, CodeMirror, Zod, Vitest, and Playwright.
- Produce the externally hosted `manifest.json`, Penpot runtime bundle, and iframe UI bundle.
- Provide a simple default workflow with:
  - HTML editor accepting a complete document or fragment.
  - Optional HTTP/HTTPS base URL for relative styles, fonts, images, and scripts.
  - Viewport preset editor.
  - Preview, diagnostics, and Import actions.
  - An advanced panel for script execution, capture delay, and detailed warnings.
- Do not persist source, credentials, or telemetry. Keep pasted content in memory only.
- Disable JavaScript by default. Enabling it requires a per-session “trusted source” confirmation explaining that sandboxing prevents Penpot access but cannot guarantee protection from infinite loops or resource exhaustion.

### Sandboxed capture engine

- Render each viewport sequentially in a nested opaque-origin iframe using `sandbox="allow-scripts"` without same-origin, navigation, forms, popups, downloads, or frame permissions.
- Inject a restrictive CSP, no-referrer policy, `<base>` URL, capture runtime, and animation-freeze stylesheet.
- With scripts disabled, nonce only the capture runtime and block all supplied scripts. With scripts enabled, explicitly nonce supplied scripts and allow their referenced network resources.
- Settle capture after DOM readiness, fonts and decodable images, two stable animation frames, and an optional delay; stop waiting after ten seconds and report incomplete assets.
- Traverse visible DOM, pseudo-elements, text ranges, stacking contexts, clipping, computed styles, bounding rectangles, scroll dimensions, and resolved asset URLs.
- Capture the initial `scrollY=0` state only. Fixed and sticky elements appear once at their initial rendered positions; interactions, hover states, animations, and navigation are not recreated.
- Validate and size-limit every message leaving the sandbox. Warn at 5,000 output layers or 30,000px document height and require confirmation; refuse above 20,000 layers, 100,000px, or a 25MB scene graph.

### Scene graph and Penpot conversion

Introduce shared, versioned TypeScript contracts:

- `CaptureRequest`: source, base URL, viewport list, script policy, and settling options.
- `ViewportSpec`: stable ID, board name, width, and viewport height.
- `SceneDocument`: viewport/document bounds, ordered nodes, deduplicated assets, and diagnostics.
- `SceneNode`: source locator, hierarchy, semantic name, geometry, stacking order, paint, text runs, layout data, asset reference, and fallback policy.
- `AssetRef`: URL, inline bytes, SVG, MIME type, dimensions, and CORS/raster eligibility.
- `Diagnostic`: severity, code, source locator, viewport, explanation, and fallback taken.
- `HostMessage`: schema-versioned capture, import, progress, cancellation, completion, and error messages.

Conversion behavior:

- Create one clipped top-level board per viewport, using the rendered document height, named `Page — Desktop 1440`, etc., and arrange boards horizontally with a 120px gap at the current viewport location.
- Preserve DOM hierarchy and meaningful layer names. Attach import ID, viewport, source locator, original tag/ID/classes, and fallback reason through plugin data.
- Map compatible CSS flex/grid containers to nested Penpot boards with native layouts. Preserve direction, wrapping, tracks, gaps, padding, alignment, sizing, and absolute children when supported; use measured constraints/geometry when native layout cannot reproduce the capture.
- Convert backgrounds, linear/radial gradients, borders, individual radii, shadows, opacity, supported blend/blur modes, clipping, rotations, and basic transforms to native properties.
- Convert rendered text runs to editable Penpot text with font family, size, weight, style, line height, letter spacing, decoration, case, alignment, and color. Preserve the requested font in metadata and warn when Penpot must substitute it.
- Upload URL/data images once per import and reproduce object-fit/cropping with image fills and clipping. Convert inline SVG through Penpot’s SVG-with-images API.
- Represent `::before` and `::after` content as named child layers.
- Rasterize the smallest unsupported subtree through an SVG/foreign-object canvas path only when all required resources are inline or CORS-readable.
- For canvas, video, iframe, complex filters/masks, unsupported transforms, or CORS-blocked rasterization, insert a measured, labeled placeholder and add an actionable diagnostic instead of aborting.
- Process shapes in bounded batches, update progress, and check cancellation between batches.
- Wrap a successful import in one Penpot undo block. Track top-level boards and remove them on cancellation or failure so partial imports are not left behind. Penpot explicitly supports grouping operations into one undo action. ([History API](https://doc.plugins.penpot.app/interfaces/HistoryContext))

## Test Plan

- Unit-test HTML preparation, base-URL resolution, CSP/script rewriting, schema validation, text-run extraction, CSS normalization, layout mapping, asset deduplication, naming, and diagnostic generation.
- Run capture integration tests in Chromium against fixtures covering marketing pages, dashboards, documentation, forms, tables, responsive media queries, flex, grid, absolute/fixed content, pseudo-elements, gradients, SVG, missing fonts/assets, long pages, and opt-in JavaScript rendering.
- Test hostile inputs: navigation attempts, form submission, popup/frame creation, oversized messages, malformed scene graphs, message spoofing, and script timeout warnings.
- Mock the Penpot API to verify exact layer hierarchy, native properties, fallback selection, batching, cancellation cleanup, and one-step undo behavior.
- Add self-hosted Penpot end-to-end tests that load the development manifest, import fixtures, inspect generated shapes, and render generated Penpot markup for comparison.
- Visual acceptance: on the supported fixture suite with identical available fonts/assets, achieve average SSIM ≥ `0.95`, no fixture below `0.90`, and no missing primary text or images without a corresponding diagnostic.
- Performance acceptance on a reference Chromium environment: capture a 5,000-layer/30,000px fixture within 10 seconds excluding remote-asset latency, import it within 30 seconds, keep progress responsive, and leave no boards after cancellation.

## Assumptions and Boundaries

- V1 targets common single-page marketing, application, dashboard, documentation, and form layouts—not arbitrary sites or multiple linked pages.
- Input is pasted HTML/CSS plus an optional base URL; URL crawling, file bundles, and ZIP uploads are deferred.
- Remote assets are requested directly by the user’s browser and may expose normal request metadata to their hosts; failures are diagnosed rather than proxied.
- JavaScript execution is trusted-source, opt-in, and best-effort. It renders one settled state but does not recreate behavior.
- Penpot components, reusable design tokens, and cross-viewport component linking are deferred; each viewport produces an independently editable board.
- No backend, LLM, analytics, or automatic content upload is introduced.
</proposed_plan>
